L92: ## Clinical research at SASH
L93: 
L94: SASH conducts no harm research which is undertaken following ethics approval. The inclusion of patients in studies is on a voluntary basis and done following consultation and with the approval of pet owners.
L95: 
L96: SASH’s primary duty is to pets and pet owners. As such, it is important to note that patient care is paramount and will always take precedence over research needs.
L97: SASH is accredited as a veterinary research establishment, and all prospective research is approved by an external ethics committee.
L98: 
L99: Our research is lead by 【63†Dr Joanna White】, who holds a PhD, a Masters of Veterinary Science majoring in Veterinary Epidemiology and is a registered Small Animal Internal Medicine Specialist.
L100: Joanna is experienced in research study design, has been published in a number of leading veterinary journals, is an examiner at Fellowship level for the Australasian College of Veterinary Scientists in both internal and feline medicine and is currently Australia’s representative on the International Renal Interest Society.
L101: Research at SASH is supported by global animal health companies, such as IDEXX and charities such as the 【64†Australian Companion Animal Health Foundation†acahf.org】 (ACAHF), part of the Australian Small 【65†Animal Veterinary Association†www.ava.com.au】 and the Australian College of Veterinary Science specialist’s training grants.
L102: ## Examples of SASH clinical research
L103: ### Medicine
L104:   * Improved use of antibiotics to treat urinary tract infections (cystitis) to guide clinical decision-making.
L105:   * Investigating the link between age and risk of dehydration in cats. This may help reduce health issues associated with older cats during hot Australian summers.
L106:   * Optimising the use of radioactive iodine to treat hyperthryoidism, a very common hormonal problem in cats. This research aims to improve long term outcomes.
L107:   * Determining the impact of general anaesthetic on kidney function of cats with chronic kidney disease.
L108:   * Identifying risk factors associated with kidney stones, to help prevent this serious and painful condition in pets.
L109: ### Surgery
L110: 
L111:   *  World first research investigating the impact Double Pelvic Osteotomy (DPO), a form of surgery, for the treatment for canine hip dysplasia.
L112: 
L113: ### Rehabilitation
L114: 
L115:   *  Using exercise tolerance testing as a predictor of quality of life and survival in cancer patients.
L116: 
L117: ### Ophthalmology
L118: 
L119:   *  The use of how advanced imaging such as MRI and CT can be used to differentiate between causes of orbital disease, a condition that affects the eye socket.
L120: ### Oncology
L121: 
L122:   * The use of a combination of two chemotherapy medications and its effects in treating aggressive mast cell tumours.

L22: Treatment of Metastic Osteosarcoma
L23: New clinical trials have commenced at five Veterinary Oncology Specialist Centres within Australia for the trial of a drug to inhibit the spread of bone cancer.  The drug Auranofin has been tested in a mouse model with  results showing a significant reduction in the spread of osteosarcoma to the lungs without any side effects. It is hoped that similar results in the reduction of metastasis will be found with dogs.
L24: Auranofin also has the potential for the prevention and treatment of osteosarcoma in humans as well as dogs. Human hospitals are also participating in this study and are listed on the information sheet.
L25: The drug Auranofin will be free but there will be costs that owners will need to pay for themselves.  These other costs include those for monitoring the osteosarcoma such as blood tests, xrays and any other testing that the oncologist recommends.  Details of the expected cost will be provided when you contact the centres participating in the trial.
L26: If you have a dog with osteosarcoma and would like your dog to be considered for this trial please contact the Veterinary Oncology Centres listed in the five states participating in this trial:

L160: ## Clinical Research
L161: 
L162: ## Clinical Research at MediPaws
L163: ##### Our commitment to advancing the field of veterinary medicine
L164: 
L165: Advancing veterinary care is about delivering the best care today while learning how to improve care for future patients. Much like in human medicine, clinical research plays an important role in helping veterinarians refine treatments, reduce risk, and achieve better patient outcomes.
L166: Many of the treatments and approaches used at MediPaws and other veterinary hospitals have been shaped by ongoing research. Through these evidence-based findings, we are able to continually improve the safety and effectiveness of care for our beloved pets.
L167: ##### Why participate in clinical research
L168: 
L169: Many pet owners participate in clinical research knowing that their pet’s involvement may help improve care for other pets in the future. By participating in our no-harm studies, your pet can contribute to better treatments, reduced procedure risk, and improved quality of life for pets in the future around the world.
L170: Each study will provide specific information about any potential benefits for your pet. Depending on the research, this may include additional insight into recovery, monitoring, or complementary diagnostic testing.
L171: 
L172: Why we're involved in clinical research​
L173: At MediPaws, clinical research is a natural extension of our commitment to provide the highest standard of care possible. Every day, our teams manage complex emergency and referral cases across multiple specialties, giving us valuable insight into how treatments perform in real-world settings and what works best.
L174: 
L175: Clinical research allows our specialists to keep asking important questions, including:
L176:   * How can we improve tests and treatments already in use?
L177:   * Can we reduce risks around anaesthesia, hospitalisation and recovery?
L178:   * What can we do to improve long-term outcomes and quality of life for patients?
L179: 
L180: What “no-harm” clinical research means at MediPaws
L181: Our specialists take a no-harm approach to all clinical research, meaning every study is designed with patient welfare as the top priority. Research is carefully structured so it never compromises care, and often involves non-invasive data collection alongside routine treatment or comparing standard approaches already in use.
L182: 
L183: Participation in any research at MediPaws is always:
L184:   * Voluntary – clear explanations are provided, and informed consent is required
L185:   * Ethics-approved – studies follow appropriate governance and ethics processes
L186:   * Patient-first – your pet’s clinical care always takes precedence over research
L187: 
L188: What does taking part in a study mean for your pet?
L189: 
L190: If your pet is eligible for a clinical study, express your interest on our study page and a member of the MediPaws team will discuss it with you in detail. As a part of this, we’ll explain:
L191:   * What the study is aiming to achieve
L192:   * What (if anything) will be different from standard care
L193:   * Answers to any questions you may have before you decide to take part
L194: 
L195: In most cases, participation does not change your pet’s treatment plan. Your pet will continue to receive the same high standard of veterinary care, monitoring, and support they would receive outside of a study. You are also free to withdraw from a study at any time, without affecting your pet’s care in any way.
L196: Your pet’s comfort, safety, and wellbeing will always be our first priority.

L55: # Foundation
L56: ##
L57: 
L58: Foundation【44†admin】2026-06-02T00:38:23+10:00
L59: 
L60: The Australian Animal Cancer Foundation supports scientific research into cancer in companion animals such as dogs and cats.  It funds equipment and expertise to treat animals with pre-existing cancer, simultaneously documenting valuable clinical information to help uncover the mysteries of cancer in both animals and humans.
L61: Importantly, The Foundation provides for clinical trials ethically evaluating new treatments for animals with cancer ultimately translating fundamental scientific research from the laboratory bench to the pet and to the bedside of human cancer patients.
L62: 
L63: To find out more about the Australian Animal Cancer Foundation go to 【45†animalcancer.com.au†www.animalcancer.com.au】.
L64: ## BVSC + The Australian Animal Cancer Foundation Current Research Projects
L65: 
L66: Surgical Oncology + Radiation Oncology + Medical Oncology
L67: 
L68: Brisbane Veterinary Specialist Centre (BVSC) is a hospital dedicated to treating cancer and to finding a cure.
L69: BVSC has always been at the forefront of oncology in Australia, being the first in the southern hemisphere to have a dedicated radiation oncology team and in-house radiation equipment. BVSC’s dedication in the field of oncology continues today, having successfully treated 1000’s of cancer patients along with the various ONCOLOGY RESEARCH that BVSC is aligned with.
